speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in respect of the recently concluded landmark Treaty on Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (a) what is the Government’s assessment of the outcome of the negotiations leading to the agreed terms of the Treaty; (b) what is the Government’s assessment of the benefits of the Treaty for Singapore; and (c) how can Singapore and Singaporeans contribute to further the objectives of the Treaty.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There has been significant concern for many years about the degradation of the marine environment and the depletion of resources in the high seas and the deep seabed.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This refers to the waters and the seabed beyond the 200-nautical-mile exclusive economic zone and continental shelf of countries and, therefore, it is beyond the jurisdiction of any particular country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is an urgent need for collective action to address the urgent threats confronting our oceans, including the issues of climate change and biodiversity loss.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The BBNJ Treaty is, thus, a historic achievement and a critical boost for global efforts to protect the marine environment.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, the Treaty enables a more holistic regulation of the marine environment in areas beyond national jurisdiction.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has hitherto been fragmented across different regional and sectoral organisations overseeing individual issues, such as fisheries management and maritime shipping.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It will fill some of these regulatory gaps, it will promote coordination across the different regional and sectoral bodies and provide greater clarity on what is required for the assessment of environmental impacts for activities in these areas.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are proud that a Singaporean, the Ambassador for Oceans and Law of the Sea Issues, Ms Rena Lee, presided over the five Intergovernmental Conference sessions, which were held between 2018 and 2023; and that this successfully led to the conclusion of the Treaty negotiations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Rena's able and tireless leadership during this long and arduous process brought countries together towards achieving a consensus outcome and reaffirmed Singapore's position as a trusted interlocutor and bridge-builder as well as underlying our leading role in developing the international law of the sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The successful conclusion of the negotiations is also a strong affirmation that multilateralism remains effective and relevant, and that a rules-based international order is needed more than ever before to resolve global issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These outcomes are relevant and beneficial to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: By codifying scientific best practices across jurisdictions and giving effect to the principle of open science, the BBNJ Treaty will augment our Institutes of Higher Learning as well as maritime companies' access to deep sea samples, thereby creating new opportunities for our research and development sector.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Through the Treaty, our scientists working with repositories such as the Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum in the National University of Singapore and agencies like the Agency for Science and Technology Research as well as the National Research Foundation will find it easier to obtain access to information and to samples of the marine organisms for their research.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore can also contribute to the objectives of the Treaty in a variety of ways.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the immediate term, we can work with other countries and regional and international organisations towards the early ratification and the effective implementation of the Treaty.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the longer term, we can support capacity-building efforts for developing countries by sharing our experience and expertise through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Singapore Cooperation Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans can contribute to combatting climate change and protecting our own environment and oceans by living sustainably and practising zero-waste lifestyles.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To conclude, the oceans, whether they lie within exclusive economic zones or in the high seas beyond national jurisdiction, are all inter-connected.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The waters and the marine biodiversity in them move freely across borders.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This means that, whatever happens in the areas beyond national jurisdiction can and will have an impact on us in Singapore – be it in terms of biodiversity loss, environmental degradation or the ocean-climate nexus.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are, therefore, privileged and honoured to have been able to play a part in ensuring the conservation and sustainable use of our oceans through the BBNJ Treaty negotiations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will certainly continue to support this crucial endeavour.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The first is this: the signing of the Treaty is only the beginning; the devil is in the details.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And there are a number of details to agree to, in the coming months, if not longer.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: As we know, in international law, the initial agreement of the Treaty is just a first step.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: It is important that all countries will also ratify and introduce – in their local laws – in as short as possible a time, so that we can all start reaping the benefits of the Treaty.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, will the Minister share with the House, what he sees as some of the challenges in getting as many countries to sign up and ratify, so that the Treaty can be properly enforced sooner rather than later?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This is especially so, given the competitive nature of the world fisheries and mining industries.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The second supplementary question: how would the Government encourage or even ensure that Singaporean businesses will only source from sustainable fisheries and undersea mining, in compliance with the requirement of this convention?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It will require, at the domestic level, policies and legislation and programmes to do so.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I will not underestimate the effort needed to persuade everyone to come on board.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why I have dealt with this at some length because, in fact, we need not just within Singapore, but across the world for everyone to understand why the oceans and the marine biodiversity in the high seas and on the seabed, the natural resources in a sense – the natural heritage of all mankind – is important and worthy of protection.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: To be honest with you, this requires political support.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am glad that at least in the case of Singapore, I think in this House, I can say that it is unanimous support for the protection of the environment for dealing with climate change, for conserving marine biodiversity and, equally important, a fair and equitable approach to how we extract resources sustainably, in areas both within our own jurisdiction, as well as areas outside.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The point is, I am very grateful for your support, but I am also saying that there will be challenges internationally.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Third, training capacity building, which will also require sharing between countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And in the case of Singapore, one of the most important programmes that we run on the international front is capacity building; in the sense of uplifting, as many across the board that we can – 	officials, students, scientists – we will continue to do so.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I would also say, we do need transparency.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Which actually brings me to the second point – how do you ensure compliance?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because these are the areas which are beyond jurisdiction.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I will not trivialise how difficult it will be to hold people to account.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I believe that if there is broad-based public support in all countries and we have a system with sufficient transparency, so, you know which companies or which institutions, what they are doing, where and the impact of their activities, I think that transparency will help ensure compliance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, again, I just want to say that I am grateful for Members' interest in this area and for Members' support, and I hope this is the same situation in parliaments all over the world.
